Local Objective Function L(x): The Tier 2 system prompt requests local stability, low wear and immediate operational goals. Prompt priority is a testable instruction, not a guarantee. Independent deterministic protections enforce the configured physical constraints.

Arbitration via Token Priorities: When local preservation conflicts with global demand, the intended SLM response to [CELL-TEMP-CRIT] is to curtail an [AGGRESSIVE-DISCHARGE] request. Measure whether the model actually proposes [SAFE-MODE-CURTAIL]. Log proposal errors separately from interlock overrides and committed actions; a protective interlock must not hide a failed arbitration decision.

3. Execution Guardrails (The Deterministic Step): A compiled C/C++ matrix or bounded verifier checks configured limits before actuation (Sha, 2001; Nesti et al., 2026). Valid numeric values outside bounds are clamped; malformed output is dropped. In-range parameter combinations can still destabilize a plant. State-dependent interlocks or validated gain regions, when used, are separately declared experimental mechanisms.

Three design principles are proposed for resilient execution: (1) state isolation through deterministic interlocks; (2) shared global/local context with explicit local survival behavior during communication loss; and (3) graceful degradation under CPU or memory strain, with independently running classical controllers and protocol maps. These mechanisms require validation under the declared operating conditions. They do not guarantee defect-free execution or stable closed-loop behavior merely by being present.

Byte-to-Token Compilation & SunSpec Mapping: Parse the transport deterministically. The RTU request 01 03 00 20 00 02 C5 C1 has CRC-16/Modbus bytes low-first and maps to read/slave/register/count tokens after CRC validation. Modbus TCP uses MBAP framing, without the RTU CRC. Discover SunSpec model IDs and lengths before interpreting registers; raw byte values alone do not identify their device semantics.
